title: Claude Managed Agents
content:
## What Is Claude Managed Agents?

Claude Managed Agents is Anthropic's hosted platform for building, deploying, and operating production AI agents at scale. Launched alongside Claude Opus 4.7 in April 2026, it extends the tool-use API with persistent memory, long-running sessions, built-in evaluation loops, and multiagent coordination — all observable through the Claude Console.

---

## Dreaming (Research Preview)

Dreaming is a scheduled background process that reviews completed agent sessions and memory stores, extracts recurring patterns, and writes curated summaries back to long-term memory. This lets agents improve over time without manual retraining or explicit human feedback.

Announced May 6, 2026. Early production results from **Harvey** (legal AI platform): agents with dreaming enabled retained file-type workarounds and tool-specific heuristics from earlier runs, resulting in approximately a **6× improvement in task completion rates** during internal testing.

Dreaming runs on a configurable schedule (e.g., nightly) rather than per-session, so the benefit compounds across many runs — an agent deployed for weeks outperforms a freshly instantiated agent on the same class of tasks.

---

## Outcomes

Outcomes let you define a **rubric** for what a correct result looks like. After an agent completes a task, a separate grader model evaluates the output against the rubric and triggers revision cycles until the result passes — or a configured retry limit is reached.

In Anthropic's internal testing, outcomes improved task success rates by **up to 10 percentage points** over standard prompting loops, with the largest gains on harder, open-ended problems.

This is distinct from simply asking Claude to self-critique: the grader is an independent model call using the rubric as its system prompt, not a self-referential continuation of the original session.

---

## Multiagent Orchestration

A lead agent can decompose a job and delegate sub-tasks to specialist agents, each configured with its own model, system prompt, and tool set. Specialists run in parallel on a shared filesystem and contribute results back into the lead agent's context window.

This enables workflows that exceed what a single context window can handle — for example:
- Auditing a large codebase by spinning up one specialist agent per module
- Processing a corpus of documents where each document gets a dedicated reviewer
- Parallelizing research tasks that would otherwise run sequentially

All agent activity — including delegation trees and inter-agent messages — is traceable through the **Claude Console**.

---

## Webhooks

Configure a webhook URL on any agent task. When the task completes or fails, the platform fires a POST to that URL with the outcome payload. This enables fire-and-forget invocation: submit a task, continue other work, and receive notification when the agent finishes. No polling required.

Webhooks can be combined with Outcomes so the notification payload includes whether the grader passed or failed and which revision cycle produced the accepted result.

---

## Claude Console

The web UI for configuring and monitoring Managed Agents deployments:
- Session logs with per-tool-call traces
- Agent configuration editor (model, system prompt, tool access, memory store)
- Outcome rubric editor
- Multiagent orchestration diagram showing delegation hierarchy

---

## Claude Design

Launched alongside Opus 4.7 as an Anthropic Labs product, **Claude Design** lets users collaborate with Claude to create visual outputs: UI mockups, presentation slides, one-pagers, and interactive prototypes. It is built on Managed Agents infrastructure and accessible from the Claude.ai interface.
